changes: Derived Spear_Thrust clip retains licensed Punch_Right body movement and Idle_Sword arm guard, with Babylon BoneIKController for both hands.
Arm controllers solve in model space to handle the imported mirrored root. The original weapon remains attached to the right wrist; the left palm follows its shaft.
Anticipation, extension, hold and recovery use the gameplay attack clock. Contact shares that clock instead of a separate countdown that could advance on the input frame.
Opening slash contact is 42 percent, distant sweep 37.5 percent, thrust 52 percent and kick 55 percent of their respective clips.
Spear reach is 3.1 instead of 3.6 units; kick reach 2.3 instead of 2.8. The thrust has a narrower forward cone and 1.5-unit vertical separation limit.
limits: Contact still uses authored attack volumes and native Havok scenery queries rather than an animated weapon mesh sweep.
The existing low-detail hero and mixed creature art remain below the requested visual standard.
Native geometry and automated completion do not establish human enjoyment or first-time chapter duration.
All tests are silent; audible impact quality remains unreviewed.
driverChange: Use throws when target vertical separation exceeds 1.5 units, and close into the shorter melee reach. The prior melee-first policy could suppress R while swinging below a flyer; no health, teleportation or enemy nerfs were added.
performanceLimits: Sequential samples varied with machine state. Arm IK p95 fell from 2.8 ms to 0.4 ms after removing redundant skeleton preparation; overall frame times did not improve in these samples. Optimized existing-session mean interval 33.76 ms / p95 55.1 / max 221.9; fresh-session 36.27 / 73.6 / 357.8. Compiled keyboard sample averaged 49.54 FPS with p95 42.4 ms. Sustained frame pacing remains open.
